[2026-08-28T04:27:03.699Z] [player] Ask about their people
[2026-08-28T04:27:03.700Z] [world] "No name, before you ask twice." A very small smile. "A name is a thing that can be put on a list. I draw the lists. I know what they are for."
[2026-08-28T04:27:03.706Z] [world] There is ink on The Cartographer's knuckle, fresh enough to still be wet at the edge.
[2026-08-28T04:27:04.398Z] [player] Ask why they serve
[2026-08-28T04:27:04.399Z] [world] The Cartographer gives you a look that measures the question for irony and finds none. "Because somebody stands at this desk, and the last one who stood here was worse. That is the honest shape of it. You do not serve because the cause is clean — no cause is clean. You serve because you have seen the desk emp
ty, and empty is worse."
[2026-08-28T04:27:04.400Z] [world] The Cartographer uses your name in the middle of it without making anything of it.
[2026-08-28T04:27:05.365Z] [player] Ask what the post has cost them
[2026-08-28T04:27:05.366Z] [world] "Friends, in the ordinary way — people hear the title before they hear me now." The Cartographer straightens something on the desk. "But the real price is smaller and dearer: I have not said a careless sentence in nine years. Every word weighed, every joke checked for edges. You are hearing the loosest I get, and you will notice I am still watching the door."
[2026-08-28T04:27:05.367Z] [world] The Cartographer keeps a finger in a page the whole time, on the chance that you turn out to be brief.
